title: Turkey, light or dark meat, smoked, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Smoked turkey is poultry meat that has been cured and slowly smoked at low temperature. Both light (breast) and dark (thigh, drumstick) meat can be used. The skin is usually removed before smoking and is not part of the finished product.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Smoking gives the meat a distinctive aroma and extends its shelf life.
Light turkey meat contains less fat than dark meat, but both are high‑protein foods.
Smoked turkey is a traditional component of holiday spreads and appetizers.
Smoked products are often served cold, but can also be reheated or added to salads.
Turkey is one of the most popular protein sources in weight‑loss oriented diets.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Smoked turkey provides about 25–30 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low fat in light meat
items.content: Turkey breast contains very little saturated fat, making it suitable for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Turkey meat is high in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, essential for bones, immunity and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low carbohydrate content
items.content: Smoked turkey contains virtually no carbs, fitting well into low‑carb eating plans.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Smoked meat products often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey proteins.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Improper smoking can lead to formation of carcinogenic compounds, so choose reputable brands.

items.title: Nitrite presence
items.content: Nitrites are sometimes added for color and preservation; excessive intake should be avoided.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Smoked turkey can be enjoyed as a cold snack, sliced thin for sandwiches, added to salads, pastas, or used in hot dishes such as casseroles, stews and soups. Trim any visible fat before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep smoked turkey refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C, where it remains good for up to 3 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration – signs of spoilage.
